..
Issued at 255 PM EDT Sat Aug 15 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Ridging overhead in the process of being dispatched stage right into 
northeastern NOAM. Double barrel shortwave setup to traverse the 
region later tonight into Sunday: a primary wave over Manitoba that 
will pass to the north of Lake Superior, and a convectively charged 
wave associated with a stationary front (the one that has been 
causing high end hydro issues across Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio the 
last week) that will lift north into southern Michigan Sunday. 
Anticipation is that the stationary front will remain well to the 
south, suppressing deeper moisture (surface dewpoints into the 
mid 70s) south of the area, but nonetheless anticipation is we 
see dewpoints spike into the upper 60s to lower 70s (so it's 
still gonna be a bit humid here), especially the farther south 
and east one goes in the CWA. Passage of the primary shortwave 
will force a cold front through the region. Coupled with 
decreasing 500mb heights and diffluence aloft, instability 
should be readily available with modest synoptic forcing to 
generate a convective response across the region. Associated 
convection / thunderstorm activity will carry on Sunday 
afternoon before the cold front passes and high pressure returns
for a short period on Monday. Progressive flow regime makes a 
comeback next week, reinforced by digging longwave troughing 
over Hudson Bay. Initial likely convectively charged wave 
passages anticipated around midweek before aforementioned 
longwave troughing digs farther south and settles into 
northeastern NOAM, with the Great Lakes right on the western 
periphery of the feature. 

Details: 

Wedge of drier air to play heck on rain chances today, as the 
primary deeper moisture axis suppresses northward advancement of 
moisture to downstate... as evidenced by visible satellite, which 
showcases a mid level cloud deck sharply cutting off right near the 
M-55 corridor. Current thinking is that this plume of cloud cover 
eventually does advance northward through tonight, and perhaps a 
shower materializes across the far southern reaches of the CWA. 
Additional support from the northern stream wave should drive shower 
and perhaps thunder activity in eastern upper later tonight as the 
core of forcing and moisture approaches. Sunday looks to be the day 
for transient downpours as PWATs surge to the 1.50-1.75 range, 
complete with skinny CAPE profiles (essentially screaming that the 
atmosphere is juiced and probably gonna turn loose). Best overlap of 
forcing, instability, and moisture will come in two phases... the 
morning hours over eastern upper should see help from elevated 
convection owing to LLJ processes. Transient downpours could easily 
drop a quick localized 1.00"+, but overall, there should be enough 
storm motion to eschew hydro issues for our friends north of the Big 
Bridge. Should be noted... there is potential for some places in 
eastern upper to get skipped by rain. 

Storm coverage over far northern and northwest lower to remain much 
more isolated through the morning into the afternoon. Front to pass 
through during peak heating the farther south and east one goes, 
coupled with subtle Lake Huron generated boundaries amid S to SSE 
flow. Result should be a pronounced uptick in convection across far 
northeast lower amid an increasingly moist profile. As such, while 
much of northern lower sees isolated downpours, the area generally 
along and east of a Cheboygan to Tawas line poses the greatest risk 
for repeated downpours, and, while not specifically outlooked by 
SPC, wouldn't be surprising to see a locally stronger to marginally 
severe storm (primary concerns wind and hail) considering some 
guidance throwing instability values in excess of 1500 J/kg right 
during the frontal passage and peak shear. As far as rainfall and 
amounts go... anticipate some places west of I-75 (in particular the 
farther south one goes) to hold dry through Sunday, with isolated 
downpours producing localized totals of 0.50-1.00"+. In northeast 
lower, storm coverage will be greater, so there will be less "rain 
gaps", indicating more spatial coverage of at least 0.10-0.25" of 
rainfall than the rest of northern lower. In the aforementioned 
highlighted area of northeast lower, potential for repeated 
downpours does pose a risk for localized 2.00"+ rainfalls over a 
short duration of time, but here too, anticipation is that downpours 
will be transient enough to dissuade hydro concerns on much more 
than a marginal, localized level.

Looking ahead, high pressure returns by Monday ushering in drier and 
seasonable weather. Next system quick to return by Tuesday 
delivering another round of showers and thunderstorms to the region. 
Deeper longwave troughing to build into the region thereafter, which 
will induce seasonably cool temperatures in the low to mid 70s,
perhaps moderating to the upper 70s lower 80s by the weekend.
